safety_signals: Systolic blood pressure increased by 5.4 mm Hg vs baseline in the torcetrapib arm (off-target pressor effect)
Decreased serum potassium with increased serum sodium, bicarbonate, and aldosterone (off-target mineralocorticoid effect)

Trial terminated early for increased death and cardiac events; described as an off-target effect of torcetrapib of unknown mechanism, though adverse effects related to CETP inhibition could not be excluded
note: Agent-curated from PubMed via the Claude PubMed MCP. According to PubMed, Barter PJ et al., 'Effects of torcetrapib in patients at high risk for coronary events,' N Engl J Med 2007;357(21):2109-2122 (DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa0706628, PMID 17984165). NCT00134264 (ILLUMINATE, n=15067) was terminated for increased mortality/cardiac events. Death: HR 1.58 (95% CI 1.14-2.19); incidence 1.23% torcetrapib+atorvastatin vs 0.78% atorvastatin. Major cardiovascular event: HR 1.25 (95% CI 1.09-1.44). Both CIs exclude 1.0 (significant), so the HR-aware bucket grades them STRONG/MODERATE rather than WEAK/AMBIGUOUS from the tiny absolute rate delta. BP/electrolyte/aldosterone are continuous off-target findings kept as safety_signals.
